We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need leaves commercially available, total price <=9999 (we can't check price but assume buyable). Need to construct route using templates.

We have some buyable building blocks: Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1 (p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride), Nc1ccc(N)cc1 (p-phenylenediamine?), actually that's an aniline with amine at para? SMILES: Nc1ccc(N)cc1 is p-phenylenediamine (two amines). Also C=CC(=O)Cl (acryloyl chloride). All are buyable.

Goal: target has a sulfonamide linking a tolyl sulfonyl group to a phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So we can think retrosynthesis:

Step 1: Disconnection of sulfonamide bond: target -> sulfonyl chloride (p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride) + aniline (the rest of molecule). The rest is: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 (a phenyl ring with para substituent being the unsaturated amide). That phenyl is attached via sulfonamide to the tolyl sulfonyl chloride. So we need an aniline (para-aminophenyl) with the unsaturated amide attached.

Thus we can propose: Starting from p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (commercial) and aniline derivative (4-aminophenyl with the unsaturated amide). The sulfonyl chloride reacts with amine to give sulfonamide.

Step 2: The aniline derivative can be formed by amide coupling of acryloyl chloride with 4-aminophenyl (aniline) to give acryloyl anilide, then maybe further functionalization? Actually the target has /C=C/ (trans) between phenyl and carbonyl: it's a cinnamamide: phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2? Wait structure: /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). So the unsaturated amide is attached to the phenyl ring via the double bond (styryl amide). So the phenyl ring (the second phenyl) is attached to the double bond (C=C) which is attached to carbonyl attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So the amide nitrogen is attached to an aniline (para-aminophenyl). So the amide is formed between acryloyl chloride and p-phenylenediamine (or aniline with amine). Actually we need a secondary amide where the nitrogen is attached to a phenyl ring bearing an amine (aniline). So we could start from acryloyl chloride + p-phenylenediamine (which has two amines). Reaction of acryloyl chloride with one amine gives the acryloyl anilide (with free amine left). That matches the target: the amide nitrogen attached to phenyl with an NH2 substituent (para). So step 2: acryloyl chloride + p-phenylenediamine -> acryloyl anilide (C=CC(=O)Nc1ccc(N)cc1). This is the fragment we need.

Thus overall route:

Leaf 1: C=CC(=O)Cl (acryloyl chloride) (buyable)
Leaf 2: Nc1ccc(N)cc1 (p-phenylenediamine) (buyable)
